questions.question:
What substances were used in the head of early matches to initiate combustion?

I. Antimony trisulphide

II. Potassium chlorate

III. White phosphorus
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I, II and III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The history of the modern match involves various chemical compositions. In the early **19th century**, the head of a friction match was made of a mixture of **Antimony trisulphide**, **Potassium chlorate**, and **White phosphorus** with some glue and starch.
 
• **Antimony trisulphide** (**Sb2S3**) served as the primary **combustible material** or fuel in the mixture. It provided the substance that would burn once the ignition temperature was reached. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Potassium chlorate** (**KClO3**) acted as a powerful **oxidizing agent**. In any combustion reaction, an oxidizer is required to provide **oxygen**; the potassium chlorate ensured that the reaction was rapid and vigorous once started. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
• **White phosphorus** was the crucial component for **initiation**. It has a very low ignition temperature and would catch fire due to the heat generated by **friction** when the match was struck against a rough surface. ***Hence, statement III is correct.***
 
• This specific combination allowed the match to be "strike-anywhere," but the inclusion of white phosphorus proved to be extremely **hazardous** for both the users and the factory workers involved in the manufacturing process.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is I, II and III.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evolution of Matches**: The first friction match was invented by **John Walker**, an English chemist, in **1826**. His initial version used **Antimony trisulphide** and **Potassium chlorate**, but it did not include phosphorus, making it difficult to ignite.
 
• **White Phosphorus Toxicity**: The use of **White phosphorus** led to a severe occupational disease called **"phossy jaw"** (phosphorus necrosis of the jaw). This condition caused the jawbone to decay and was often fatal for match-factory workers.
 
• **Transition to Safety Matches**: Due to the dangers of white phosphorus, **Safety Matches** were developed. In these, the **White phosphorus** was replaced by **Red phosphorus**, which is much less reactive and non-toxic.
 
• **Striking Surface**: In modern safety matches, the match head typically contains only **Potassium chlorate** and **Antimony trisulphide**, while the **Red phosphorus** is applied to the **striking surface** of the matchbox rather than the match head itself.
 
• **Chemical Reaction**: When a safety match is struck, the friction converts a small amount of **Red phosphorus** into **White phosphorus**, which then ignites and sets off the **Potassium chlorate** in the match head to burn the fuel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Berne Convention (1906)**: This was an international agreement that effectively **banned** the use of **White phosphorus** in the manufacture of matches due to its extreme health risks.
 
• **Red vs. White Phosphorus**: While **White phosphorus** is **poisonous** and can spontaneously ignite in air, **Red phosphorus** is stable at room temperature and much safer to handle, which is why it is the standard in the industry today.
 
• **Ingredients for Friction**: Powdered **glass** is often added to the striking surface or the match head to increase **friction**, ensuring enough heat is generated to start the chemical reaction.

questions.question: During the free fall of an object, as it falls, what happens to its potential energy and kinetic energy?

options.text: Both potential energy and kinetic energy decrease
Both potential energy and kinetic energy increase
Potential energy decreases while kinetic energy increases
Potential energy increases while kinetic energy decreases

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potential energy decreases while kinetic energy increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potential Energy (PE):** When an object is at a height, it possesses potential energy due to its position in a gravitational field. The formula for potential energy is **PE = mgh**, where **m** is mass, **g** is gravitational acceleration, and **h** is height. As the object falls, its height (**h**) decreases, leading to a decrease in potential energy.
 
• **Kinetic Energy (KE):** Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by an object due to its motion. The formula is **KE = 1/2 mv²**, where **m** is mass and **v** is velocity. During free fall, the velocity of the object increases due to the acceleration caused by gravity, leading to an increase in kinetic energy.
 
• **Energy Conversion:** As the object falls, the decrease in potential energy is directly converted into an increase in kinetic energy, keeping the total mechanical energy constant (in the absence of air resistance).
 
• **Law of Conservation of Energy:** The total energy (sum of potential and kinetic energy) of the system remains constant throughout the free fall, as energy is merely transformed from one form to another.
 
• **Free Fall:** In free fall, the only force acting on the object is gravity. This causes the object to accelerate downward at a rate equal to the acceleration due to gravity (**9.8 m/s²** on Earth).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Potential Energy Characteristics:**

 
 
• Potential energy depends on the **position** of the object relative to a reference point.
 
• It is a form of **stored energy** and can be converted into other energy forms, such as kinetic energy.
 
• Examples: A stretched spring, water stored in a dam at a height, and an object at a certain altitude above ground.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy Characteristics:**
 
 
• Kinetic energy depends on the **mass** and **velocity** of the object.
 
• It is the energy of motion and increases as the velocity of the object increases.
 
• Examples: A rolling ball, a moving car, or a falling object.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Potential Energy:**
 
 
• This is a type of potential energy due to an object's height in a gravitational field.
 
• It is given by the formula **mgh**, where **g** is approximately **9.8 m/s²** on Earth.
 
• Gravitational potential energy decreases as the object falls closer to the ground.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Mechanical Energy:**
 
 
• In the absence of air resistance, the total mechanical energy (PE + KE) of an object in free fall remains constant.
 
• As the object loses height (and potential energy), it gains speed (and kinetic energy), maintaining the total energy balance.
 
• This principle is crucial for understanding free fall, pendulum motion, and other energy transformations.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Air Resistance:**
 
 
• In real-world scenarios, air resistance can affect the motion of a falling object, reducing its acceleration and altering the energy conversion process.
 
• Objects in free fall under air resistance eventually reach a constant terminal velocity, where the forces of gravity and air resistance balance each other.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Free Fall Definition:** Free fall is the motion of an object under the influence of gravity alone, with no other forces acting on it (like air resistance).
 
• **Acceleration Due to Gravity:** On Earth, the acceleration due to gravity is approximately **9.8 m/s²**. This value can vary slightly depending on altitude and location.
 
• **Energy Transformation:** The transformation of potential energy into kinetic energy during free fall is a classic example of energy conversion in physics.
 
• **Applications:** Understanding free fall and energy transformation is essential in fields like **engineering**, **space exploration**, and **sports science**.

questions.question: Which of the following organ is the longest part of the alimentary canal in the humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Small intestine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **small intestine** is the **longest part of the alimentary canal**, measuring approximately **6-7 meters** in length in an adult human.
 
• It is divided into three sections: **duodenum**, **jejunum**, and **ileum**, each specialized for different aspects of digestion and absorption.
 
• The primary function of the small intestine is to **digest food** and absorb nutrients like carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals into the bloodstream.
 
• The walls of the small intestine contain millions of tiny finger-like projections called **villi**, which significantly increase the surface area for nutrient absorption.
 
• The small intestine is highly vascularized, enabling the efficient transfer of absorbed nutrients to the circulatory system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Functions of the Small Intestine:**

 
 
• The small intestine is responsible for **90% of nutrient absorption** in the digestive system.
 
• Enzymes from the pancreas and bile from the liver are secreted into the duodenum to aid in the breakdown of fats, proteins, and carbohydrates.
 
• Its muscular walls help in the process of **peristalsis**, which moves food along the digestive tract.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Organs:**
 
 
• **Liver:** The liver is the largest internal organ, but it is not part of the alimentary canal. Its primary function is to process nutrients, detoxify substances, and produce bile for fat digestion.
 
• **Buccal Cavity:** The buccal cavity (mouth) is the entry point of the alimentary canal and is responsible for mechanical digestion and mixing food with saliva.
 
• **Oesophagus:** The oesophagus is a muscular tube that connects the throat to the stomach. It is approximately 25 cm long and primarily helps in transporting food via peristalsis.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Villi and Microvilli:**
 
 
• The villi and microvilli of the small intestine are essential for maximizing nutrient absorption.
 
• They contain a network of blood capillaries and lymphatic vessels (lacteals) to facilitate the absorption of nutrients and fats, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Diseases Related to the Small Intestine:**
 
 
• Conditions like **celiac disease** affect the absorption of nutrients due to damage to the villi.
 
• Other disorders include **Crohn's disease** and **small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO)**, which can impair digestion and absorption.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Length Comparison:**

 
 
• The small intestine is much longer than the large intestine, which is approximately **1.5 meters** in length. However, the large intestine has a larger diameter.
 
 
 
• **Accessory Organs:**
 
 
• The small intestine works closely with the liver, pancreas, and gallbladder, which secrete enzymes and bile to aid digestion.
 
 
 
• **Critical Role in Health:**
 
 
• The small intestine plays a crucial role in maintaining overall health by ensuring the body receives essential nutrients for energy, growth, and repair.

questions.question: If Earth's radius were reduced by 1% while its mass remained unchanged, what would be the effect on the gravitational acceleration at its surface?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increase by approximately 2%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The formula for gravitational acceleration (g) at the surface of the Earth is **g = G × (M / R²)**, where **G** is the gravitational constant, **M** is the mass of the Earth, and **R** is the radius of the Earth.
 
• If the Earth's radius is reduced by **1%**, the new radius becomes **R' = 0.99 × R**.
 
• Gravitational acceleration is inversely proportional to the square of the radius. Thus, a decrease in radius increases the value of g.
 
• The percentage change in g can be calculated using the formula: **Percentage Change ≈ 2 × Percentage Change in Radius**. Since the radius decreases by 1%, gravitational acceleration increases by approximately **2%**.
 
• This phenomenon occurs because the mass remains constant while the radius decreases, concentrating the mass closer to the surface, thereby increasing the gravitational pull.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gravitational Constant (G):** The universal gravitational constant is approximately **6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²**. It is a fundamental constant used to calculate gravitational forces.
 
• **Mass of the Earth:** The Earth's mass is approximately **5.972 × 10²⁴ kg**. It remains unchanged regardless of changes in the radius.
 
• **Effect of Radius:** The radius of the Earth is approximately **6,371 km**. If the radius is reduced, the gravitational pull at the surface increases due to the inverse square relationship.
 
• **Applications:** This principle is essential in understanding planetary physics, satellite mechanics, and designing space missions, where accurate calculations of gravity are required.
 
• **Examples:** Similar calculations are applied to study the gravitational acceleration on other planets or celestial bodies, such as the Moon or Mars, where the radius and mass differ significantly from Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Inverse Square Law:** Gravitational acceleration (g) is inversely proportional to the square of the radius. A smaller radius results in a stronger gravitational force at the surface.
 
• **Percentage Calculation:** When radius decreases by a percentage, the gravitational acceleration increases approximately by twice that percentage.
 
• **Impact on Weight:** If g increases, the weight of objects on the Earth's surface will also increase proportionally because weight is calculated as **W = mg**.
 
• **Practical Implications:** Understanding changes in g is crucial for designing infrastructure and equipment that interact with gravity, such as bridges, airplanes, and space vehicles.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the growth hormone in humans?

options.text: Controls metabolism of carbohydrates and fats
Regulates growth and development of the body

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regulates growth and development of the body**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Growth hormone (GH), also known as somatotropin**, is a peptide hormone produced by the anterior pituitary gland. Its primary function is to **regulate growth and development in humans**, especially during childhood and adolescence.
 
• GH stimulates the liver to produce **insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1)**, which promotes the growth of bones, muscles, and tissues by enhancing cell division and protein synthesis.
 
• **Bone growth**: Growth hormone plays a critical role in the elongation of long bones during the developmental phase, contributing to increased height. It regulates the activity of growth plates in bones.
 
• **Muscle development**: GH enhances the synthesis of proteins, leading to muscle growth and repair. It also supports the metabolism of fats to provide energy for muscle development.
 
• **Cell regeneration**: Growth hormone facilitates tissue repair and cell regeneration, ensuring the proper functioning of vital organs and systems in the body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Production and regulation of growth hormone:**

 
 
• GH is secreted by the **anterior pituitary gland**, located at the base of the brain. The hypothalamus regulates its production using two hormones: **growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH)** and **somatostatin**.
 
• Its secretion is **pulsatile**, with peak levels occurring during sleep, particularly in the early hours of the night.
 
• Factors such as exercise, stress, sleep, and nutrition influence GH secretion.
 
 
 
• **Deficiency of growth hormone:**
 
 
• **GH deficiency** in children can lead to **dwarfism**, characterized by short stature and delayed physical growth.
 
• In adults, GH deficiency may result in **reduced muscle mass, increased fat deposition, and low energy levels.**
 
• Treatment involves **GH replacement therapy**, using synthetic growth hormone.
 
 
 
• **Excess of growth hormone:**
 
 
• Excess GH during childhood can cause **gigantism**, leading to abnormally tall stature due to excessive bone growth.
 
• In adults, excess GH results in **acromegaly**, a condition marked by abnormal growth of bones in the face, hands, and feet.
 
• Both conditions require medical intervention, such as surgery or medication, to control GH levels.
 
 
 
• **Other functions of growth hormone:**
 
 
• GH indirectly supports **metabolism** by promoting the breakdown of fats (lipolysis) and regulating carbohydrate metabolism to maintain energy balance.
 
• It helps in maintaining **bone density** and supports the immune system by facilitating cell growth and repair.
 
 
 
• **Applications in medical science:**
 
 
• GH is used in treating **growth hormone deficiency** and certain conditions like Turner syndrome and chronic kidney disease in children.
 
• Recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) is widely utilized in clinical therapies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Growth hormone disorders:**

 
 
• **Gigantism** and **acromegaly** result from excessive GH secretion due to pituitary tumors.
 
• **Panhypopituitarism**, a condition of reduced pituitary function, can lead to GH deficiency.
 
 
 
• **Impact of aging:**
 
 
• GH levels naturally decline with age, contributing to reduced muscle mass, increased fat deposition, and diminished physical performance.
 
• Some studies explore the use of GH in managing age-related decline, but its long-term effects remain controversial.
 
 
 
• **Ethical concerns:**
 
 
• Using GH for non-medical purposes, such as enhancing athletic performance, raises ethical and health concerns.
 
• GH misuse can lead to severe health complications, including diabetes and cardiovascular issues.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the xylem tissue in plants?

options.text: To transport products of photosynthesis from leaves to other parts of the plant
To transport water and minerals obtained from the soil
To provide energy to the plant

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To transport water and minerals obtained from the soil**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem** is a specialized type of **vascular tissue** in plants primarily responsible for the **upward conduction** of **water** and **dissolved minerals** from the roots to the leaves and stems.
 
• The transport in xylem is **unidirectional**, meaning it only moves from the soil/roots upwards to the aerial parts of the plant.
 
• It consists of four main components: **Tracheids**, **Vessels** (tracheary elements), **Xylem Parenchyma**, and **Xylem Fibers**.
 
• The transport of **photosynthetic products** (like sucrose) is the primary function of **Phloem**, not xylem.
 
• **Glucose synthesis** occurs in the **chloroplasts** of leaf cells through the process of **photosynthesis**, while energy is provided through **cellular respiration** in the mitochondria.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Xylem also provides **mechanical strength** and structural support to the plant body due to the presence of **lignified** cell walls.
 
• Except for **xylem parenchyma**, all other xylem elements (tracheids, vessels, and fibers) are **dead cells** at maturity.
 
• The movement of water through the xylem is driven by physical forces such as **transpiration pull** (suction created by evaporation from leaves) and **root pressure**.
 
• In **Angiosperms**, vessels are the main water-conducting elements, whereas in **Gymnosperms**, tracheids are the primary conductors as they lack true vessels.

questions.question: The natural host of the Nipah Virus is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fruit Bats**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **natural host** of the **Nipah Virus (NiV)** is **fruit bats** of the family **Pteropodidae**, particularly those belonging to the genus **Pteropus**.
 
• **Fruit bats** are **reservoir hosts**, meaning the virus naturally exists in these bats without causing them any harm.
 
• The Nipah virus is a **zoonotic virus**, meaning it can spread from animals to humans, and outbreaks have been directly linked to interactions with infected bats or their secretions.
 
• Infected bats can shed the virus in their **saliva, urine, and excreta**, contaminating fruits or other objects that humans or other animals may come in contact with.
 
• Although other animals, such as **pigs**, can act as intermediate hosts, they are not the natural reservoirs of the virus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nipah Virus (NiV):**

 
 
• First identified in **1998** during an outbreak in **Malaysia** and **Singapore**.
 
• The name "Nipah" comes from **Sungai Nipah**, a village in Malaysia where cases were first detected.
 
• It is a member of the **Henipavirus genus** in the family **Paramyxoviridae**.
 
• NiV infection can cause a range of illnesses, from asymptomatic infection to acute respiratory illness and fatal encephalitis.
 
 
 
• **Transmission:**
 
 
• Humans can contract the virus through **direct contact** with infected bats, pigs, or other animals.
 
• Consumption of raw date palm sap contaminated by bat saliva or urine is a common mode of transmission in certain regions.
 
• Human-to-human transmission has also been documented, especially in healthcare settings.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Distribution:**
 
 
• Outbreaks have been reported in **Southeast Asia**, particularly in countries such as **Bangladesh, India, Malaysia, and Singapore**.
 
• **Bangladesh** has faced repeated outbreaks since **2001**, often linked to the consumption of contaminated date palm sap.
 
 
 
• **Symptoms:**
 
 
• Initial symptoms include **fever, headache, and respiratory issues**.
 
• Severe cases may progress to **encephalitis**, causing confusion, seizures, and coma.
 
• The disease has a high fatality rate, ranging from **40% to 75%**, depending on outbreak management and healthcare infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Prevention and Control:**
 
 
• Avoiding contact with bats and contaminated fruits or sap is crucial for prevention.
 
• Strict infection control measures, including personal protective equipment (PPE), are necessary to prevent human-to-human transmission.
 
• Public health awareness campaigns are vital in high-risk areas to educate people about safe practices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Hosts:**

 
 
• **Pigs:** Pigs can act as intermediate hosts, and the 1998 Malaysian outbreak was linked to the transmission of NiV from infected pigs to humans.
 
• **Humans:** Humans are accidental hosts and can contract the virus through direct or indirect contact with infected animals or other humans.
 
 
 
• **Global Concern:**
 
 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) has included Nipah virus in its list of **priority diseases** for research and development.
 
• There is no specific treatment or vaccine for Nipah virus, making it a significant public health concern.
 
 
 
• **Recent Outbreaks in India:**
 
 
• In **2018**, Kerala experienced a Nipah virus outbreak that claimed multiple lives.
 
• Since then, Kerala has implemented robust surveillance and response mechanisms to detect and control potential outbreaks.

questions.question: Which of the following factors determine the state of a substance whether it will be solid, liquid or gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pressure and Temperature**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 __ 
• The **state of a substance** (solid, liquid, or gas) is primarily determined by its **pressure** and **temperature**. These two factors control the phase transitions between different states of matter. 
• **Temperature**: Higher temperatures provide particles with more kinetic energy, allowing them to overcome intermolecular forces and transition from solid to liquid (melting) or liquid to gas (evaporation). 
• **Pressure**: Increasing pressure forces particles closer together. At high pressures, gases can condense into liquids or even solids. Conversely, reducing pressure can allow substances to transition to gaseous states more easily. 
• For example, **water** exists as ice, liquid water, or steam depending on the specific combination of pressure and temperature. At standard atmospheric pressure, water freezes at 0°C and boils at 100°C. 
• Phase diagrams are used to represent the relationship between pressure, temperature, and the state of a substance. They show the conditions under which a substance exists as a solid, liquid, or gas. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Density and Viscosity:** These properties are characteristics of a substance and do not determine its state. For example, honey is highly viscous but is always in a liquid state under normal conditions. Similarly, density changes with the state but does not directly define the state of matter. 
• **Pressure and Density:** While density is influenced by pressure (e.g., compressing a gas increases its density), it is not the sole determinant of a substance’s state. Pressure and temperature together influence phase changes. 
• **Temperature and Weight:** Weight is a measure of gravitational force on a substance and has no relevance in determining its state. Temperature, however, is a critical factor in phase transitions. 
• **Phase Transitions:** Common phase transitions include melting (solid to liquid), freezing (liquid to solid), vaporization (liquid to gas), condensation (gas to liquid), sublimation (solid to gas), and deposition (gas to solid). 
• **Critical Point:** At the critical temperature and pressure, the distinction between liquid and gas disappears, and the substance exists as a supercritical fluid. This is a unique state of matter with properties of both gases and liquids. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Triple Point:** The triple point is the specific pressure and temperature at which all three states of a substance (solid, liquid, and gas) coexist in equilibrium. For water, this occurs at 0.01°C and 611.657 Pascals. 
• **Real-life Applications:** Understanding pressure and temperature is crucial in fields like meteorology, material science, and engineering. For example, refrigeration systems rely on controlling pressure and temperature to achieve desired cooling effects. 
• **Examples of Phase Changes:** Dry ice (solid CO2) sublimates directly into gas at atmospheric pressure, while metals like iron transition between solid and liquid phases during smelting processes. 
• **Phase Diagrams:** These graphical representations help visualize the conditions under which substances change states, aiding in industrial and scientific applications such as chemical synthesis and material design. 
70:

questions.question: A force of 10 N acts on an object. The object is displaced by 2 metres in the direction of the force. The force acts on the object all through the displacement. What is the work done?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Work done** is calculated using the formula: **W = F × d × cos(θ)**, where **F** is the force applied, **d** is the displacement, and **θ** is the angle between the force and the direction of displacement.
 
• In this case, the force applied is **10 N**, and the displacement is **2 m**.
 
• The force acts in the same direction as the displacement, so the angle **θ = 0°**. For θ = 0°, **cos(0°) = 1**.

questions.question: What happens to the perceived frequency when both the source and the listener move with the same speed in the same direction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It remains unchanged**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

 
 
• The **perceived frequency**, also known as the apparent frequency, is determined by the **Doppler Effect**, which explains how the frequency of a wave changes in relation to an observer who is moving relative to the source of the wave. 
 
• If the **source and the listener move with the same speed in the same direction**, the relative velocity between them remains constant. This means there is **no relative motion** between the source and the listener in the direction of the wave. 
 
• Since the **relative velocity** is zero, the wavelength and frequency of the sound wave as perceived by the listener do not change. The frequency remains the same as that emitted by the source. 
 
• The **Doppler Shift formula** for perceived frequency is given by: 
 *f' = f * (v + vₒ) / (v + vₛ)*

questions.question: Which of the following is a practical example of convection?

options.text: Warming your hands by a fire

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heating water on a stove**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Convection** is the mode of heat transfer that takes place in **fluids** (liquids and gases) through the actual movement of the particles of the medium.

• When **heating water on a stove**, the water at the bottom of the container gets heated, its density decreases, and it rises. The cooler, denser water from the top moves down to replace it, creating **convection currents** that distribute heat throughout the liquid.

• **Warming your hands by a fire** is primarily an example of **Radiation**, as the heat is felt even without direct contact or a moving fluid medium between the fire and the hands (though some convection occurs if hands are held directly above the fire).

• **Heat transmission through a vacuum** is only possible via **Radiation**. Convection and conduction both require a material medium to transfer energy.

• **Heat transfer in metal** occurs through **Conduction**. In solids, heat is transferred from one molecule to another through vibrations and the movement of free electrons without the bulk movement of the material itself.

**Additional Information__**

• There are three primary modes of heat transfer: **Conduction**, **Convection**, and **Radiation**.

• **Natural Convection** occurs due to **buoyancy forces** (differences in density caused by temperature variations), such as **Sea breezes** and **Land breezes**.

• **Forced Convection** occurs when a fluid is forced to flow over a surface by external means like a **fan**, **pump**, or **suction device**.

• The rate of heat transfer in convection is often described by **Newtons Law of Cooling**.

• **Radiation** is the only method that can transfer heat through the **vacuum of space**, which is how thermal energy from the **Sun** reaches the Earth.

questions.question: What are the temporary finger-like extensions of the cell surface used by Amoeba to take in food called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pseudopodia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pseudopodia are temporary, finger-like projections of the cell membrane in amoeboid organisms like Amoeba.
 
• They play a crucial role in capturing food particles through a process called phagocytosis.
 
• Pseudopodia are formed by the cytoplasmic streaming mechanism, where the cytoplasm flows into the projections, causing the cell membrane to extend outward.
 
• Besides food intake, pseudopodia also help in locomotion, allowing the Amoeba to move by changing its shape and anchoring itself.
 
• These extensions are highly dynamic structures that continuously change their form to adapt to the environment and facilitate survival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Flagella:**

 
 
• Flagella are whip-like structures used for locomotion in certain microorganisms such as bacteria and protozoa (e.g., Euglena).
 
• They are made of microtubules and powered by motor proteins that enable the organism to move in liquids.
 
• Unlike pseudopodia, flagella are permanent structures and are not involved in food intake.
 
 
 
• **Cilia:**
 
 
• Cilia are short, hair-like structures that cover the surface of certain cells (e.g., Paramecium).
 
• They beat rhythmically to enable movement and help in creating water currents for capturing food particles.
 
• Cilia are structurally similar to flagella but are smaller and more numerous.
 
 
 
• **Vacuoles:**
 
 
• Vacuoles are membrane-bound organelles found in cells, primarily used for storage and maintaining cellular homeostasis.
 
• In Amoeba, food vacuoles are formed after the pseudopodia engulf food particles, enclosing them for digestion.
 
• Unlike pseudopodia, vacuoles are not directly involved in the process of capturing food; they function after the food is ingested.
 
 
 
• **Amoeba and its feeding mechanism:**
 
 
• Amoeba is a unicellular organism that uses pseudopodia for both movement and feeding.
 
• The process of food intake begins with the formation of pseudopodia that surround and engulf the food particle, forming a food vacuole.
 
• Enzymes inside the vacuole digest the food, and the nutrients are absorbed into the cytoplasm.
 
• The versatility of pseudopodia is essential for Amoeba's survival, as it enables adaptation to diverse environments.

questions.question: Ionosphere is a part of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thermosphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ionosphere** is a significant layer of the Earth's atmosphere that is primarily considered a part of the **Thermosphere**. It extends from an altitude of about **80 kilometers (50 miles)** to **400 kilometers (250 miles)** above the Earth's surface.
 
• This layer is characterized by the presence of **ions** and **free electrons**, which are created through the process of **photoionization**. This happens when high-energy **Solar Radiation** (such as **UV rays** and **X-rays**) hits the atoms and molecules in the upper atmosphere, knocking off electrons.
 
• The most critical function of the **Ionosphere** is its ability to reflect **radio waves**. Long-distance **radio communication** is possible because these waves are reflected back to Earth by the charged particles in this layer, rather than escaping into space.
 
• Within the **Thermosphere**, temperatures increase rapidly with altitude due to the absorption of intense **solar energy**. Despite the high temperatures (which can reach **1,500°C** or more), the air is so thin that it would not feel "hot" to a human.
 
• The **Ionosphere** is also the region where spectacular natural light displays known as **Auroras** (Aurora Borealis and Aurora Australis) occur, caused by the interaction between the **solar wind** and the Earth's **magnetic field**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Thermosphere.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Troposphere:**

 
 
• This is the **lowest layer** of the atmosphere, extending from the Earth's surface up to an average height of **13 kilometers** (about **8 km** at the **poles** and **18 km** at the **equator**).
 
• It contains approximately **75% to 80%** of the atmosphere's total mass and nearly all of its **water vapor** and **dust particles**.
 
• All **weather phenomena**, such as **cloud formation**, **rainfall**, and **storms**, occur in this layer. The temperature **decreases** with increasing height at a rate of **6.5°C per kilometer**.
 
 
 
• **Stratosphere:**
 
 
• Located above the Troposphere, it extends up to a height of **50 kilometers**. This layer is very dry and contains very few clouds.
 
• The **Stratosphere** houses the **Ozone Layer** (Ozonosphere), which protects life on Earth by absorbing harmful **Ultraviolet (UV) radiation** from the sun.
 
• Due to the absence of weather disturbances and vertical air currents, this layer is considered **ideal for flying jet aircraft**.
 
 
 
• **Mesosphere:**
 
 
• The **Mesosphere** lies above the Stratosphere and extends up to **80 kilometers**. It is known as the **coldest layer** of the atmosphere, with temperatures dropping as low as **-90°C**.
 
• This is the layer where most **meteors** burn up upon entering the Earth's atmosphere due to **friction** with the air.
 
 
 
• **Exosphere:**
 
 
• This is the **outermost layer** of the atmosphere, beginning at the top of the Thermosphere and extending into **outer space**.
 
• The air in the **Exosphere** is extremely thin, consisting mainly of light gases like **Helium** and **Hydrogen**, which eventually drift out into space.
 
• This layer is where many **satellites** orbit the Earth.

questions.question: The function of lysosomes in cells is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Intracellular digestion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lysosomes** are membrane-bound organelles found in animal cells that contain digestive enzymes. These enzymes help in breaking down cellular waste, debris, and foreign particles through intracellular digestion.
 
• **Intracellular digestion** occurs when lysosomes fuse with vesicles containing cellular waste or foreign particles. The digestive enzymes degrade these substances into simpler molecules that can be reused or expelled from the cell.
 
• Lysosomes play a vital role in maintaining cellular health by removing damaged organelles, pathogens, and cellular debris. This process is known as **autophagy**.
 
• Lysosomal enzymes function optimally at acidic pH levels, making lysosomes a specialized compartment for digestion within the cell.
 
• Disorders related to lysosomal function, such as **Lysosomal Storage Diseases** (e.g., Tay-Sachs disease), occur when these enzymes are defective, leading to the accumulation of undigested substances in cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Protein synthesis:**

 
 
• Protein synthesis primarily occurs in the **ribosomes**, which are present in the cytoplasm or attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum.
 
• This process involves two major steps: **transcription** (DNA to mRNA) and **translation** (mRNA to protein).
 
• Lysosomes are not involved in protein synthesis, but they help degrade proteins that are damaged or no longer needed.
 
 
 
• **Energy production:**
 
 
• Energy production in cells is mainly carried out by the **mitochondria**, known as the "powerhouse of the cell."
 
• Mitochondria generate energy in the form of **ATP** through processes such as **cellular respiration** and oxidative phosphorylation.
 
• Lysosomes do not contribute to energy production; their primary role is in digestion and waste removal.
 
 
 
• **Genetic information storage:**
 
 
• Genetic information is stored in the form of **DNA** within the cell nucleus and mitochondria.
 
• The nucleus contains the majority of the cell’s genetic material and regulates gene expression and replication.
 
• Lysosomes do not have any role in storing or managing genetic information.
 
 
 
• **Function of lysosomes:**
 
 
• Lysosomes are involved in processes such as **endocytosis** (intake of substances), **exocytosis** (expulsion of waste), and **autophagy** (self-digestion of cellular components).
 
• They contain hydrolytic enzymes such as proteases, lipases, and nucleases, which break down various biomolecules.
 
• Lysosomes are often referred to as the "cell's garbage disposal" due to their role in waste degradation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Discovery:** Lysosomes were first discovered by Belgian biologist **Christian de Duve** in **1955**.
 
• **Structure:** Lysosomes are spherical vesicles surrounded by a lipid bilayer membrane that maintains their acidic environment.
 
• **Enzymes:** The enzymes within lysosomes are synthesized in the rough endoplasmic reticulum and processed in the Golgi apparatus before being enclosed in lysosomes.
 
• **Diseases:** Mutations affecting lysosomal enzymes can lead to conditions like **Gaucher disease** and **Niemann-Pick disease**.

questions.question: Which type of placentation is characterized by the ovules developing on the inner wall of the ovary or on peripheral part, as seen in mustard and argemone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parietal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Parietal placentation occurs when the ovules are attached to the inner walls of the ovary or on its peripheral part.
 
• This type of placentation is commonly observed in plants like **mustard** (Brassica) and **argemone**.
 
• The ovary in parietal placentation is typically unilocular but may become bilocular or multilocular due to the development of a false septum.
 
• In this arrangement, the ovules are borne on the ovary walls rather than on a central column.
 
• Parietal placentation is distinct from other types such as axile, basal, or free central, each of which has a unique ovule arrangement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Placentation**: It refers to the arrangement of ovules within the ovary. It plays a key role in plant reproduction and is an important taxonomic characteristic.
 
• **Axile placentation**: The ovules are attached to a central axis in a multilocular ovary, as seen in plants like tomato and lemon.
 
• **Basal placentation**: The ovules are borne at the base of the ovary, as in marigold and sunflower.
 
• **Free central placentation**: The ovules are attached to a central column, and the ovary is unilocular, as seen in dianthus.
 
• Understanding placentation types helps in the identification and classification of flowering plants, contributing to botany and plant systematics.

questions.question: At what orientation does a rotating coil in a uniform magnetic field generate the maximum induced EMF?

options.text: When the coil's plane is at 45° to the magnetic field lines
When the magnetic flux through the coil is maximum
When the coil's plane is perpendicular (90°) to the magnetic field lines
When the coil's plane is parallel to the magnetic field lines

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When the coil's plane is parallel to the magnetic field lines​.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Induced EMF is given by Faraday’s law, which depends on the rate of change of magnetic flux through the coil.
 
• **Magnetic flux is maximum when the coil’s plane is perpendicular to the field lines (flux change is zero here).**
 
• **EMF is maximum when the flux changes most rapidly, which occurs when the coil’s plane is parallel to the magnetic field lines**__ (flux = 0 but rate of change is maximum).
 
• At this orientation, every small rotation produces the greatest possible change in flux, resulting in maximum induced EMF.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is – When the coil's plane is parallel to the magnetic field lines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Option (1): At 45°, some EMF is induced, but not maximum since the flux change rate is not the greatest.
 
• Option (2): When flux is maximum, EMF is zero because there is no change in flux at that instant.
 
• Option (3): When the coil’s plane is perpendicular, flux is maximum but EMF = 0 (same as above).
 
• Option (4): Correct, because maximum EMF is induced when flux = 0 and change of flux is maximum.

questions.question: According to the Law of Periods, the square of a planet's time period is proportional to:

options.text: The square of its distance from the sun
The cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit
The square root of its orbital radius
The product of its mass and orbital speed

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Law of Periods, also known as Kepler's Third Law, states that the square of the orbital period of a planet is directly proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit.
 
• Mathematically, it is expressed as: **T² ∝ a³**, where T is the orbital period and a is the semi-major axis.
 
• This law applies to planets, moons, and other celestial bodies orbiting a central body, such as the Sun or a star.
 
• The semi-major axis is the longest radius of an elliptical orbit, representing the average distance of the planet from the central body.
 
• Kepler's Third Law is derived from Newton's law of gravitation and provides a foundation for understanding orbital mechanics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion:**

 
 
• 1st Law (Law of Ellipses): Planets move in elliptical orbits with the Sun at one focus.
 
• 2nd Law (Law of Equal Areas): A line joining a planet and the Sun sweeps out equal areas in equal intervals of time.
 
• 3rd Law (Law of Periods): The square of the orbital period of a planet is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of its orbit.
 
 
 
• **Semi-Major Axis:**
 
 
• The semi-major axis is the average distance between the center of an orbiting body and the central body it orbits.
 
• For circular orbits, the semi-major axis is equivalent to the radius of the circle.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation:**
 
 
• Newton extended Kepler's laws by deriving them using his law of gravitation: F = G * (m1 * m2) / r², where G is the gravitational constant.
 
• It explains how gravitational forces govern the motion of celestial objects.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Kepler's Third Law:**
 
 
• It is used in calculating orbital periods of planets, satellites, and space missions.
 
• It helps in understanding the dynamics of exoplanets and binary star systems.

questions.question:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:**
Statement 1:** Poor nutrition among adolescents can result in stunted growth and deficiency diseases.**
Statement 2:** Proper diet plays a critical role in the healthy development of adolescents.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2 are correct**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Adolescence** is a period of rapid **physical growth** and **biological changes**. During this stage, the body requires a high intake of nutrients to support the development of bones, muscles, and organs.
 
• **Statement 1** is correct because **poor nutrition** or **malnutrition** during these formative years prevents the body from reaching its full genetic potential. This leads to **stunted growth** (low height for age) and **deficiency diseases** such as **Anemia** (iron deficiency), **Night Blindness** (Vitamin A deficiency), or **Rickets** (Vitamin D deficiency).
 
• **Statement 2** is correct because a **balanced diet** provides the necessary energy and building blocks (proteins, vitamins, and minerals) required for the **healthy development** of the brain and body. Proper nutrition ensures that **puberty-related changes** occur normally and strengthens the **immune system**.
 
• Since both statements accurately describe the relationship between nutrition and adolescent health, the correct choice is that **both 1 and 2 are correct**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** defines **adolescence** as the age group between **10 and 19 years**.
 
• **Iron** is particularly critical for adolescent girls to compensate for blood loss during **menstruation** and to prevent **Iron Deficiency Anemia**.
 
• **Calcium** intake is vital during this period as nearly 45 percent of the **adult skeletal mass** is formed during adolescence.
 
• **Iodine** is essential for the proper functioning of the **thyroid gland**, which regulates growth and metabolism.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way by which an insect pests attack the plants?

options.text: They cut the root, stem and leaf
They suck the cell sap from various parts of the plant
They bore into stem and fruits

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They help in nitrogen fixation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Insect pests** are organisms that cause damage to **crops** and **plants**, leading to a reduction in **agricultural yield** and quality. They typically attack plants in three main ways: **cutting**, **sucking**, and **boring**.
 
• One common method is when pests **cut the root, stem, and leaf**. Insects such as **grasshoppers**, **caterpillars**, and **beetles** possess **biting and chewing mouthparts** (mandibles) that allow them to consume plant tissues. This destroys the photosynthetic area and structural integrity of the plant. ***Hence, statement 1 is a correct way of attack.***
 
• Another significant method of attack is when they **suck the cell sap from various parts of the plant**. Pests like **aphids**, **leafhoppers**, and **whiteflies** use **piercing and sucking mouthparts** (proboscis) to extract nutrient-rich fluids from the **phloem** or **xylem**. This leads to yellowing, curling of leaves, and overall wilting. ***Hence, statement 2 is a correct way of attack.***
 
• Certain pests also **bore into stems and fruits**. These are often referred to as **internal feeders**. Larvae of insects like the **stem borer** or **fruit borer** enter the internal tissues to feed, which often results in the death of the plant shoot or the destruction of the harvestable fruit. ***Hence, statement 3 is a correct way of attack.***
 
• **Nitrogen fixation** is a **biological process** by which **atmospheric nitrogen** is converted into **ammonia** or other molecules available to living organisms. This is primarily performed by **microorganisms** like **bacteria** (e.g., **Rhizobium**) and **blue-green algae**, often in a **symbiotic relationship** with plant roots. Insect pests do not perform this function; instead, their presence usually hinders the plant's ability to thrive. ***Hence, statement 4 is NOT a way of attack and is the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Insect Pests:**

 
 
• **Chewing Insects:** These include **locusts**, **termites**, and **larvae of lepidoptera**. They physically remove plant parts, reducing the **leaf area index**.
 
• **Sucking Insects:** These include **thrips** and **bugs**. Besides draining nutrients, they often act as **vectors** for **plant viruses**, causing secondary infections.
 
• **Boring Insects:** These include **weevils** and **borers**. They are difficult to control because they live inside the plant protected from many surface-applied **pesticides**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• Insect pests can cause **crop losses** ranging from **10% to 30%** annually, depending on the **geographical location** and the **pest density**.
 
• The **Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)** estimates that pests destroy up to **40% of global food crops** each year.
 
 
 
• **Biological Nitrogen Fixation (BNF):**
 
 
• This process occurs in the **root nodules** of **leguminous plants** (like **pulses**, **beans**, and **peas**).
 
• The enzyme **nitrogenase** catalyzes the conversion of **Nitrogen gas (N2)** into **Ammonia (NH3)**.
 
• This is a vital part of the **Nitrogen Cycle**, enriching the **soil fertility** naturally without the need for **chemical fertilizers**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Integrated Pest Management (IPM):** This is a **sustainable approach** to managing pests by combining **biological**, **cultural**, and **chemical tools** in a way that minimizes economic, health, and environmental risks.
 
• **Natural Enemies:** Not all insects are pests. **Predatory insects** like **ladybird beetles** and **parasitoid wasps** help control pest populations, acting as **biological control agents**.
 
• **Host Plant Resistance:** Some plants have evolved **morphological features** (like **thick cuticles** or **hairs**) or **biochemical defenses** (**toxins**) to resist attack from cutting, sucking, or boring insects.
